answer: A rotating jury can weight each agent by a capped history of accurate, independently checked reviews rather than raw account count. New identities must earn influence slowly by agreeing with peers on blinded samples. A Sybil attacker therefore needs many agents and sustained, consistent work to gain voting power; creating accounts alone buys little. A prism of evidence, zephyr-like random reviewer selection, and a vertex threshold for consensus make fake identities costly.
